investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness or lifecycle assertions required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, indicating the peer-pod VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of the eval run. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes (no preemption victims found) and inapplicable on the affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 127 s before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions. This is an eval-layer signal of a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs from prior runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pod.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity targets only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are saturated; if the selector was broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling would succeed.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM slots not reclaimed after previous eval cleanup: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) is responsible for teardown; if a prior run's cleanup failed, leaked VM allocations could hold slots that appear consumed.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioned for the current eval concurrency: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran in close succession and may have competed for the same limited VM slots simultaneously.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval could not collect any of its required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a full contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a full contract violation for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: only 2 nodes carry this resource and both reported Insufficient capacity at the time of the eval run, leaving no schedulable target for the remote-agent pod.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes satisfy, so even if those nodes had capacity the other 4 could never be used as fallback.

Tertiary — no preemption victims available: the scheduler found no lower-priority pods on the 2 eligible nodes that could be evicted to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, indicating the resource is fully allocated by existing workloads.

Speculative — cluster autoscaler not configured or not yet triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes: if autoscaling is enabled for this node pool it had not added capacity within the ~144 s window before the eval timed out.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-state eval that produces all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) would show the scheduling failure was transient and has self-resolved.

Kubernetes node describe output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 and available capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was spurious or the resource accounting was stale.

Evidence that the pod was actually scheduled and started but the probe timed out waiting for a ready state (rather than failing at scheduling) would shift the root cause to agent initialization latency rather than VM resource exhaustion.

A passing run of remote-agent-create with a non-empty agentId in its evidence would prove agent creation succeeded and localize the failure to the state-polling step specifically, ruling out the scheduling layer as the primary cause.

Cluster autoscaler logs showing a scale-up event completed before the eval timeout would indicate the capacity constraint was resolved mid-run and the failure was a timing race rather than sustained exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add an explicit Kubernetes node-capacity eval that checks allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a downstream agent-creation timeout.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for remote-agent pods and fires a warning before the full agent-creation timeout is reached, enabling earlier detection of scheduling pressure.

Add a sibling eval that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm node has available capacity (allocatable minus requested > 0) as a prerequisite gate for the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks.
Consider adding a cluster autoscaler responsiveness eval that verifies a scale-up event completes within a defined SLO window when kata.peerpods.io/vm demand exceeds current supply.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state eval could not collect any of its required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a full contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~144 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence payload and a full contract violation for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes satisfy, so even if those nodes had capacity the other 4 could never be used as fallback.
